packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-03 - unverified blind image reading
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview, face A)
- A narrow vertical parchment strip (approx. 2.5 cm wide x 19 cm tall by the scale), cut from a larger leaf; upper right corner cut obliquely. Displayed upright.
- Only the beginnings (or ends) of lines of a single text block survive: c. 1-2 words per line, roughly 40 lines visible.
- Script: late-medieval cursive (Bastarda/Kursive type) in brown ink; vernacular German appearance ("vnnd" repeated). No rubrics, initials or ruling observable at this scale. One line near the top third begins with a larger letter (looks like "Also"/capital), possibly a section start (tentative).
- Sewing/binding thread remnants protrude at right edge around one-third down and on left two-thirds down; a small hole/stain near the middle left. A modern pencil/ink shelfmark-like note at lower part ("...STA... 157..."?) in a different (modern) hand, over the text lines.
- Interpretation (tentative): a binding strip from a document or vernacular codex; continuous prose, one column fragment only.

SELECTED SPANS: all surviving line-fragments on both faces (the strip preserves only 1-2 words per line, so every line is read). Nothing left unread deliberately; right edge of the text is cut away throughout.

FACE A

image-002.jpg (native tile, upper half of the strip; overlaps image-003 at bottom). Crops made: c02a.jpg (lines 1-6), c02b.jpg (lines 8-13).
Lines are line-fragments; beginnings cut at left by the strip edge too (left margin not preserved, words start mid-word).
002-01  [...]bey in[...]  (or "ben in"; "y" uncertain)
002-02  [...]d Jr E[...]   (large capital J with long descender; E/B? at cut edge)
002-03  [...]la ſtũng      (horizontal loop/abbr. above u; possibly "-ſtung"; "la" uncertain)
002-04  [...]ʒ? frewnde(n)? (read "[...]rfrewnde" / "[...]freunden"; final stroke may be -n abbreviation; very uncertain)
002-05  [...]ẏ Erb z[...]  ("Erb" clear with capital E; then a z-like letter, perhaps "zu" or "7"/et-sign)
002-06  [...]ſtain? vnnd   (faint; "vnnd" fairly clear)
002-07  [...]bruch?[...]   (line below the small hole, very faint/abraded; [illegible] except "b" and "ch?")
002-08  [...] white abraded band / repair patch: [illegible]
002-09  [...]4 wiſſz? [...] (first sign looks like an arabic 4 or the end of "-t"; then "wiſſ"/"wiſſz"; uncertain)
002-10  Alls               (enlarged looped capital A; "Alls" or "Allſo"; probably a sentence/section opening, indented)
002-11  [...]ſbliche? vn[...]   (or "[...]ſolliche"/"[...]ſchliche"; then "vn" cut)
002-12  [...]nnes? azona?  (letters clear in shape but sense unclear: "aines"/"vnnes" then "azona"/"ayona"; [uncertain])
002-13  [...]nt amm[...]   ("[...]nt" then "amm"/"anm" + long s/f at cut: "ammſ[...]")
002-14  [...]nt die ham[...]  ("die" clear, then "Ham"/"haw"; could be "ſunt"/"vnt die Ham[...]")
002-15  [...]ari? . vnnd    (point after first word; "vnnd" clear)
002-16  [...]l? vnnd yt?    ("vnnd" clear; then "yt"/"ist")
002-17  [...]nnd Nar[...]   (or "vnnd daz"; capital N/D uncertain)
002-18  [...]ſtig vnnd      ("-ſtig"/"-ſtag" then "vnnd")
Note: a transparent modern repair tape spans roughly lines 14-17; a grey stain under the tape at left edge.

image-003.jpg (native tile, lower half of the same face). Overlap: lines 003-01..04 repeat 002-15..18 ("[...]ari. vnnd" / "vnnd yt" / "vnnd Nar" / "ſtig vnnd"); not counted again. Crops made: c03a.jpg (lines 5-10), c03b.jpg (lines 11-19).
003-01..04  = 002-15..18 (overlap)
003-05  [...]Recht? od[...]   (first letter R or B with loop; "-echt"/"-elht" uncertain; "od" = oder? cut)
003-06  [...]ech vnnd z[...]  ("vnnd" clear; z with long descender at cut)
003-07  [...]andern? / van[...]  (virgule after first word; second word "van"/"wa[...]")
003-08  [...]ch vnnd
003-09  [...]geſchaffen? v[...]  (left end obscured by thread; "-ſchaffen"/"-ſchoffen" fairly clear, tall ſ ascender)
003-10  [...]willigkait? [...]  (heavily faded and partly under thread; "-ligkait"/"-ligkeit" probable; interlinear above it some small marks resembling "1 3 0" - could be a modern pencil number, uncertain)
003-11  [...]ſtrimarch?    (abraded, a shiny spot in the middle; letters "ſt..m..ch" only tentative)
003-12  [...]nung verſch[...]  ("verſch" or "vorſch" at cut)
003-13  ſo mugen?            (or "ſo nugen/ſo mügen"; long s + o clear, then "mugẽ")
003-14  [...]erlihen? an[...]   ("verlihen"/"erleihen" uncertain; "an" after a point)
003-15  [...]haimte? D[...]h[...]  (modern pencil "Stams" written above/over this line; "-mte" then capital D)
003-16  [modern blue/grey pencil: "STA, Frg. 157.." - modern shelfmark, overwrites medieval line; medieval letters under it illegible]
003-17  [...]der . zuuerſ[...]  ("-der" then point, then "zuuerſ"/"zunerſ")
003-18  [...]y Deutſchn?[...]   (capital D clear; "Deutſch-"/"Durſten-" uncertain; final letters "-anta"/"-en t[...]")
Bottom of strip follows; no further lines.
Face A total: c. 32 line-fragments.

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE B (image-004.jpg, reduced overview)
- Same strip, reverse (mirror outline: oblique cut now at upper left). Surface darker, yellow-brown, stained; little or no medieval text visible at overview scale.
- A uniform grey rectangle covers the middle third of the strip (c. 6.5 cm), in the image itself (masking or a card placed over it); nothing beneath it can be seen.
- Thread remnants at left upper third; a horizontal slit/hole near the top; white spots (adhesive/paper residue) below.
- Modern pencil note at bottom: "Stams, STA / Frg. 157v" (modern shelfmark-type note; I record it as an observation only and draw no identification from it).

FACE B

image-005.jpg (native tile, upper part of face B; lower part is the grey mask). Crop made: c05a-blue-eq.jpg (blue channel, equalized, upper 620 px).
- No medieval writing visible, at native resolution or in the contrast-enhanced blue-channel crop. Surface is stained/darkened (hair or flesh side used as outer binding face); possible very faint dark smudges near the top are mottling, not letter forms.
- Features: slit and small hole c. 1/3 down; thread wrapping at left; white paper/adhesive residue spots; transparent tape at the bottom edge of the visible area, then the grey mask.
- Reading: no text. [blank or erased/abraded - cannot tell which]

image-006.jpg (native tile, lower part of face B; overlaps image-005 at top: tape edge repeated).
- Most of the tile is the grey mask (no content). Below it: stained parchment with no visible medieval writing; dark smudge marks only.
- Modern pencil at bottom: "Stams, STA / Frg. 157v".
- Reading: no medieval text visible.

LIMITATIONS AND NOTES
- Only Face A carries legible text: c. 32 line-fragments of 1-2 words each, German vernacular prose in a late-medieval cursive with frequent "vnnd"; left and right of every line cut away, so no complete word sequence beyond two words. Many readings are tentative (marked "?").
- Face B appears blank on the visible parts; the central third is hidden by a grey mask in the images themselves. A wider/unmasked view of face B would be needed to rule out text there.
- Modern pencil shelfmark notes ("Stams", "STA, Frg. 157", "157v") are on the object itself; I report them as observations only. Nothing else in my context revealed an identification.
- Beyond the brief: none. I made crops only in rscratch/packet-03 (c02a.jpg, c02b.jpg, c03a.jpg, c03b.jpg, c05a-blue-eq.jpg). Did not hit the image limit.
